channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: French Culture Days to Be Held in Bukhara
item.description: Bukhara Governor Botir Zaripov met with the French Ambassador to Uzbekistan to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. A key initiative is holding French Culture Days in Bukhara in October, showcasing French heritage, art, music, cinema, and literature. Cooperation in education and French language learning was also discussed.

item.title: Hydrogen Storage to Stabilize Autonomous Power Systems Within Seconds After Failures
item.description: Tomsk Polytechnic University scientists and Chinese researchers have developed a model for an autonomous power system using hydrogen storage. This system can quickly restore power stability after accidents or load changes, making it valuable for remote settlements and industrial sites relying on renewable energy sources.

item.title: US Invites Russia to G20 Energy Ministers Meeting in Texas
item.description: The United States has invited Russia to participate in the G20 Energy Ministers meeting scheduled for September 14-16 in Texas. A Russian official will attend the Houston summit, though the specific representative has not yet been identified.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President inaugurates bean processing plant in Talas region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov opened a bean processing plant in the Talas region. The facility, with an investment of 200 million soms, has a capacity of 40,000 tons annually and created 100 jobs. The president highlighted the region's agricultural potential and the importance of domestic processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP criticizes tree planting initiatives for focusing on quantity over quality
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has criticized environmental campaigns for prioritizing the number of trees planted over their survival rate. The focus is often on media reports showing planting, rather than ensuring long-term care and growth. Experts suggest evaluating the effectiveness of funds spent and the actual survival of saplings.

item.title: Tajikistan agency discusses anti-corruption strategy in Gorno-Badakhshan
item.description: Representatives of Tajikistan's anti-corruption agency met in Murghab district, Gorno-Badakhshan, to discuss the state anti-corruption strategy for 2030. The meeting also covered the law on combating corruption, dangers of youth involvement in extremism, and drug trafficking issues. Recommendations were given on preventing corruption and adhering to criminal and administrative laws.

item.title: Labor migrants contributed nearly $4 billion to Russia's budget in six months
item.description: Labor migrants contributed approximately $4 billion to Russia's budget in the first half of the year. This amount represents a 30% increase compared to the same period last year. The data highlights the significant financial impact of migrant labor on the Russian economy.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's main oil pipeline halted after drone attack, impacting global supply
item.description: Saudi Arabia's main oil pipeline, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, has ceased operations following a drone attack. The 1,200 km pipeline transported 4-5 million barrels of oil daily, representing 4-5% of global oil supply. The incident raises concerns about energy security in the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Scientific Organizations Can Set Prices for Their Developments
item.description: State scientific and scientific-technical organizations in Kyrgyzstan will be able to generate income from the sale of their research and development results at self-determined rates. The cabinet chairman signed a corresponding resolution. The document clarifies the right of these organizations to earn from research, educational, consulting, publishing, and commercial activities.

item.title: First South Korea-Central Asia Summit to Be Held in Seoul
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung will host the first summit with leaders from five Central Asian countries—Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan—in Seoul on September 16, 2026. The summit will focus on expanding trade and investment, energy cooperation, critical minerals, and supply chains. Bilateral meetings are scheduled for September 14-16.

item.title: Medical Union Supports Convicted Nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva
item.description: The Central Committee of the Healthcare Workers' Union of Kyrgyzstan has expressed support for nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva, stating readiness to protect her rights. The union acknowledged the family's distress and the tragic nature of the event, but urged consideration of the medical profession's specifics and the circumstances of medical decisions. Beyshebaeva was sentenced to three years in prison.

item.title: Tajik Prosecutor General Attends ECO Meeting on Combating Transnational and Cybercrime
item.description: Tajikistan's Prosecutor General, Habibullo Vohidzoda, participated in the seventh meeting of ECO Prosecutors General in Turkestan, Kazakhstan. Delegates from Azerbaijan, Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan discussed digitalization of criminal prosecution, combating cybercrime, internet fraud, cryptocurrency crimes, and the shadow economy.

item.title: Organized crime groups allegedly blocked ban on binary options in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan MP Dastan Bekeshev stated that organized crime groups influenced lawmakers, preventing a ban on binary options after its first reading. He supports a new government-initiated bill but believes its enforcement mechanism needs refinement, particularly regarding identifying financial accounts.

item.title: CIA warned of explosive-laden plane attack on US years before 9/11
item.description: The CIA has declassified intelligence reports from 1998-2001, revealing warnings about Osama bin Laden's intent to attack the US, including a scenario of a plane filled with explosives targeting a US city. Analysts noted potential disinformation and scarce details on specific targets.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Outlines Major Development Projects Including Kambar-Ata-1
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced plans to address Kyrgyzstan's electricity deficit with the Kambar-At-1 hydropower plant, aiming for domestic needs and exports. He also detailed progress on new transport routes like the Balykchy—Kochkor railway and the Barskoon—Bedel road, potentially boosting regional trade and connectivity. Development of the Ala-Too Resort ski area was also mentioned.

item.title: Korea-Central Asia Summit Elevates Partnership to Strategic Level
item.description: The first Korea-Central Asia summit marks a significant upgrade in the partnership, moving from inter-agency coordination to strategic decision-making. This elevation coincides with Uzbek President Mirziyoyev's state visit to South Korea, signaling Seoul's view of Central Asia as a key strategic partner and reflecting regional transformation.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Criticizes Compatriots Abroad for 'Mankurtism'
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov criticized some Kyrgyz citizens living abroad for exhibiting 'mankurtism,' a term implying forgetting one's history and culture, while also thanking those contributing to the economy. He made the remarks during 35th-anniversary independence celebrations in Talas. Japarov did not specify punitive measures but vowed to educate and call them to order.

item.title: Over 200 Power Workers Ensured Electricity for Independence Day Celebrations in Talas
item.description: More than 200 employees from the Talas Power Grid Enterprise ensured uninterrupted electricity supply for the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence celebrations in Talas. The company reported that lighting, sound equipment, and other technical systems operated without issues during the events, which included the opening of new facilities and a drone show.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's 36th independence anniversary to be celebrated in Naryn region
item.description: The 36th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence in 2027 will be celebrated in the Naryn region, President Sadyr Japarov announced. He stated that holding celebrations in different regions has become a tradition, with this year's festivities taking place in Talas region.

item.title: Tajikistan participates in international conference on combating internet fraud
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs reported its participation in an international conference on combating telecom and mobile fraud in Lianyungang, China, on September 10, 2026. The event, initiated by China's Ministry of Public Security, discussed terrorism, extremism, cybercrime, and internet fraud threats. Participants emphasized strengthening international cooperation.

item.title: Ecological Staff Attacked During Raid Against Illegal Sand Extraction in Guzar
item.description: An ecological department head in Uzbekistan's Qashqadaryo region was found unconscious after an attack by lawbreakers during a raid against illegal sand extraction. The incident occurred on the Qashqadaryo River. Lawbreakers resisted inspectors, injured one, and escaped with seized equipment. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Three Isfara Dried Fruit Producers Achieve International FSSC 22000 Certification
item.description: Three dried fruit producers from Isfara, Tajikistan – Isfarafood LLC, Vodii Mevakho LLC, and Oro Isfara LLC – have obtained the international FSSC 22000 certification. Supported by the Swiss-funded 'Trade Promotion to the East' project, this achievement enhances their competitiveness and market access. The certification confirms compliance with global food safety standards.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan spends billions on textbooks, yet parents still buy books for children
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated over 1.6 billion soms for new textbooks in two years, but parents report shortages and are forced to purchase books themselves. Many textbooks are of poor quality or outdated, leading parents to buy new ones for their children's education.

item.title: BRICS Summit: Modi urges Putin to negotiate peace in Ukraine
item.description: At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin, urging negotiations for peace in Ukraine. India emphasizes dialogue and diplomacy, offering support for peace efforts. The leaders also discussed the Black Sea region's stability.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Implement EMPIC GmbH Software for Flight Safety Oversight
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will adopt the EMPIC GmbH software system for flight safety oversight, according to the Civil Aviation Agency. Successful system testing has been completed. The agreement was signed by the agency head and EMPIC GmbH's representative, aiming to automate certification and supervision processes.

item.title: Turkpol Organization to be Established Among Turkic States
item.description: A proposal by Turkey's Interior Minister to establish a Turkpol Organization among Turkic states has been supported by four nations. The organization will combat crime, similar to Interpol and Europol.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews National Museum Construction and Urban Development
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev inspected the construction of the National Museum of Uzbekistan and development work in the Almazar district. He held a video conference on increasing public income, using Almazar as an example. The museum project, designed by Tadao Ando and Atelier Brückner, will be a significant cultural space.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Outlines New Approaches for Capital City Development
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on Tashkent's socio-economic development, investment, and infrastructure. New approaches are needed to utilize district potential, increase added value, and create high-paying jobs. Districts should specialize economically, with plans to attract $9 billion in investments this year.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances cooperation with ICAO on civil aviation development
item.description: Uzbekistan is expanding its partnership with the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) to boost civil aviation. Discussions focused on ICAO's role in international aviation, its activities, and collaboration with Uzbekistan. The country aims to modernize airport infrastructure and improve services to enhance tourism.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Attends Independence Day Celebrations in Talas
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov participated in large-scale celebrations in Talas marking the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence. The event featured a theatrical performance depicting the nation's history. Japarov outlined strategic goals for economic strength and national unity, announcing next year's celebration in Naryn.

item.title: France opens doors for Uzbek startups at International Space Summit
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Digital Technologies, Sherzod Shermatov, met with La French Tech to discuss strengthening tech and startup cooperation. They explored opportunities for French startups entering Uzbekistan and for Uzbek startups expanding to France and Europe. La French Tech supports startups in accessing international markets and investors. Uzbek IT Park programs were also discussed.

item.title: Uzbek Senate discusses changing borders of Zarafshan city and Tamdyn district
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan held its nineteenth plenary session in Tashkent, discussing the proposed change in borders between Zarafshan city and the Tamdyn district of Navoi region. The initiative aims to foster Zarafshan's development, attract investment, and create jobs by transferring 2,459 hectares from Tamdyn district to the city.

item.title: UNESCO: 739 Million Adults Illiterate Worldwide, Two-Thirds Are Women
item.description: According to UNESCO, 739 million adults globally are illiterate, with women constituting two-thirds of this population. Additionally, 273 million children worldwide do not attend school. UNESCO stated on International Literacy Day that this problem hinders human rights and societal development.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank and IsDB Institute Discuss Islamic Capital Platform for Central Asia
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) and the Islamic Development Bank Institute (IsDB Institute) are discussing a new mechanism to attract Islamic investment capital to Central Asian countries. The initiative aims to create a specialized structure or regional investment platform, potentially utilizing the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) infrastructure to fund small and medium-sized businesses.

item.title: Tashkent Saves 11 Million kWh of Electricity and 10 Million Cubic Meters of Gas Monthly
item.description: Tashkent has saved 11 million kWh of electricity and 10 million cubic meters of gas in one month. Officials have been instructed to systematically identify illegal constructions, ensure the rule of law, and guarantee the inevitability of punishment.

item.title: Uzbek President Visits Modern Pharmaceutical Plant in Tashkent
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the "RomPharm NS" pharmaceutical production facility in Tashkent's Almazar district. The plant aims to supply the domestic market with quality medicines and increase import substitution, with plans for a yearly capacity of 1 billion tablets and 500 million capsules. The facility, built to EU GMP standards, represents a €45 million investment and has created 150 jobs.

item.title: Shanghai Spirit Remains Key for Trust and Cooperation, Says Uzbek Official
item.description: The Shanghai Spirit continues to be vital for strengthening security, economic interaction, and sustainable development within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), according to Ulugbek Shermatov, Chairman of the Legislative Chamber Committee of Uzbekistan. He highlighted the SCO's 25th anniversary and the growing importance of China's role in Central Asia's economic resilience and trade expansion.

item.title: Earthquake in southern Lebanon follows Israeli tunnel 폭발
item.description: A seismic activity of magnitude 4.1 was recorded in southern Lebanon following an Israeli military operation that destroyed Hezbollah infrastructure. The event caused an earthquake in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Boost Textile Exports to $4 Billion by 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase its textile exports to $4 billion by the end of 2026, up from $2.6 billion in 2025. A dialogue between regulatory agencies and textile producers focused on overcoming technical barriers, implementing international standards, and enhancing export potential. Companies are advised to research target market requirements before production.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry Receives Credentials from Belgian and Swedish Ambassadors
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov received the credentials of newly appointed ambassadors from Belgium, Matthias Kende, and Sweden, Martin Rosen. Discussions focused on strengthening political dialogue, expanding trade, economic, and investment cooperation, and enhancing bilateral relations within the framework of the European Union.
